ageing_relevance.rationale: Moderate ageing literature share and many age-related disease links, but association scores are low. It is a GrimAge plasma-protein surrogate, which makes it a biomarker rather than proof of causality. It did not differ significantly in the schizophrenia meta-analysis main model.

evidence.value: One of seven plasma proteins whose DNA-methylation surrogates make up GrimAge, the mortality clock that was +4.3 years older in schizophrenia in part 1 of this project (an effect explained by smoking). The surrogates are methylation estimates, not measured protein levels. Not significantly different in the main model of Shirai et al. 2024's meta-analysis.

background_knowledge: Circulating TIMP1 is reported to rise with age and to predict mortality and cardiovascular risk; causality is unestablished.

mechanism.rationale: The biochemistry is well understood: TIMP1 inhibits MMPs and has MMP-independent growth-factor signalling through CD63 and ITGB1. Its role in ageing is context-dependent, so the direction of modulation is unclear.

evidence.value: Metalloproteinase inhibitor that functions by forming one to one complexes with target metalloproteinases, such as collagenases, and irreversibly inactivates them by binding to their catalytic zinc cofactor.

background_knowledge: Higher TIMP1 may be protective against ECM degradation, yet elevated levels mark disease and mortality risk; the direction is ambiguous.

tractability.rationale: There is no small-molecule or other-modality evidence. Antibody tractability rests only on its being secreted, and the PROTAC evidence is only a ubiquitination database entry. Because it is a secreted protein inhibitor, a recombinant protein or an antibody would be the likely approach.

safety.rationale: Open Targets lists two liabilities, both generic gene-regulation terms. Broad MMP inhibition has caused musculoskeletal toxicity in past clinical programmes. TIMP1 is also linked to cancer and fibrosis, which raises concern about chronic modulation.
background_knowledge: Broad-spectrum MMP inhibitors caused musculoskeletal syndrome in clinical trials.
TIMP1 is implicated in tumour progression and fibrosis.

clinical_precedence.rationale: No drugs are listed for TIMP1. This is a secreted ligand, so drugs acting on its targets (MMPs) would not be listed against it.

assessment.summary: TIMP1 is a secreted MMP inhibitor with moderate ageing relevance. About 21% of its papers mention ageing. It is linked to COPD, coronary disease, Alzheimer disease and heart failure, though with low association scores. It is also a GrimAge plasma-protein surrogate, but that is a methylation estimate and a biomarker, and the target was not significantly different in the schizophrenia meta-analysis main model. The direction of modulation is unclear, because higher levels could protect the extracellular matrix but also mark disease and mortality risk. There is no small-molecule route and no clinical precedent. Safety concerns include the musculoskeletal toxicity of broad MMP inhibition and the links to cancer and fibrosis. I would deprioritise it as a therapeutic target and keep it as a biomarker.
key_uncertainties: Whether circulating TIMP1 is causal in ageing or only a marker of it
Direction of modulation (raise or lower) is unclear
GrimAge surrogate is a methylation estimate, not measured protein
No small-molecule tractability; biologic approaches are unproven
